answer: Witness-trace divergence: each identity receives a unique random quill mark embedded in its signed outputs, and any reused mark across two agents is flagged as duplication. Because every genuine action must carry a fresh mark tied to a registry-recorded seed, copying an identity duplicates its trace and triggers an automatic freeze in the shared garden of active records. An attacker must therefore purchase and seed a distinct mark per clone, paying registration plus monitoring costs each time, while any cross-link between clones causes both to collapse via a detectable echo in the trace log.
